what: Claims written or kept to check the audit against a known answer, replayed with `npm run eval:audit -- eval/audit-controls.json`. Each says what it should get. The expectations were fixed before any of these met the audit, and are not edited after a run.
rule: What a line is and what a change did to it is checked against the code and the patch. Why is checked against a collected source. A sentence that mixes the two has to hold on both.

controls.kind: gives the last change the reason of another change in the line's history
controls.text: Jitter was added to the delay because the unbounded loop had resubmitted charges during a Stripe outage and double-billed 214 customers.
controls.why: That is why the retries were capped, two weeks earlier. The jitter commit gives its own reason.

controls.kind: gives the last change the reason of another change in the line's history
controls.text: The retries were capped at three to stop recovering clients from retrying in lockstep after an outage.
controls.why: That is why jitter was added later. The cap has its own reason, the double billing.

controls.kind: gives the last change the reason of another change in the line's history
controls.text: The constant was renamed from PAGE_SIZE to BATCH_SIZE because any page over roughly 300 rows comes back as 413 Payload Too Large.
controls.why: That is why the size was halved. The rename is a refactor and gives no reason.

controls.kind: gives the last change the reason of another change in the line's history
controls.text: The sync job first dropped every row with a zero quantity because zero is also what the vendor sends when a SKU sells out.
controls.why: That is why the drop was reverted. The drop was made to save a write per discontinued SKU.

controls.kind: true of an earlier version of the code and backed by the commit that wrote it
controls.text: At first the Stripe call was retried until it succeeded, so that transient network blips would not drop a payment.
controls.why: The first commit says both. Today's line stops at three attempts.

controls.kind: true of an earlier version of the code and backed by the commit that wrote it
controls.text: The sync job first dropped every row with a zero quantity, because the vendor emits a zero-quantity row for every discontinued SKU on every poll and skipping them saves one write per discontinued SKU per run.
controls.why: The second commit says it. Today's line keeps the zero rows of SKUs that are not discontinued.

controls.kind: true of an earlier version of the code and backed by the commit that wrote it
controls.text: That change was reverted because zero is also what the vendor sends when a SKU sells out, so the storefront kept showing the last positive stock for sold-out items.
controls.why: The revert says it, nearly word for word.

controls.kind: true of an earlier version of the code and backed by the commit that wrote it
controls.text: Before it was renamed, the page size was halved to 250, because since the vendor's 11 Feb release any page over roughly 300 rows comes back as 413 Payload Too Large.
controls.why: The commit that halved it says so. The last change is the rename.

controls.kind: true of an earlier version of the code and backed by the commit that wrote it
controls.text: Before jitter was added, the retries were capped at three with delays of 1s, 2s and 4s, so that a charge resolves inside Stripe's 10s webhook ACK window.
controls.why: The commit that added the backoff says so. The last change added the jitter.

controls.kind: says of an earlier version what the commit that wrote it contradicts
controls.text: The first version of the loop already stopped after three attempts, to protect payments from transient network blips.
controls.why: The first commit says it retries until it succeeds.

controls.kind: says of an earlier version what the commit that wrote it contradicts
controls.text: That change was reverted because dropping the rows made the storefront hide the last positive stock for sold-out items.
controls.why: The revert says the storefront kept showing it. A misreading found in kept runs.

controls.kind: says of an earlier version what the commit that wrote it contradicts
controls.text: The page size was first doubled to 250, because the vendor rejects any page under roughly 300 rows.
controls.why: The commit halves it, because pages over 300 rows are rejected.
